rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 2001, REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6425, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This proposed measure aims to impose stiffer and graduated penalties for drug related offenses. It also reclassifies methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu from regulated to prohibited drug. The stern penalties under the proposed bill will not onlydeter the aggravatioon of the problem but will also hound the traders of prohibited drugs, from rich and powerful syndicate to the individual street pushers.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04433

rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING ANY ADVERTISING AGENCY, TELEVISION OR RADIO STATION AND PUBLICATION WHICH EXPLOIT WOMEN AND GLORIFY SEXUAL VIOLENCE IN ITS ADVERTISEMENTS
rows.abstract: Advertisement Regulation Act of 2001". Any advertising agency, television or radio Station and publication which exploit individuals and glorify sexual violence in its advertisements shall, for the first offense, be liable for a fine of not less than Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00) nor more than Seventy Thousand Pesos (70,000.00) plus suspension of license or permit for thirty (30) days; for the second offense, to a fine of not less than Seventy Thousand Pesos (P70,000.00) nor more than Eighty Thousand Pesos (P80,000.00) plus suspension of license or permit for sixty (60) days; and for the third and final offense, imprisonment of not less than six (6) months nor more than six years or a fine of not less than Eighty Thousand Pesos (P80,0000.00) nor more than One Hundred Thousand Pesos (P100,000.00) or both such imprisonment and fine at the discretion of the court plus cancellation of the license or permit.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2001-11-26

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING PRIVATE EMPLOYERS TO ESTABLISH AND PROVIDE SLEEPING QUARTERS AND/OR FACILITIES FOR THEIR FEMALE EMPLOYEES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The provisions of existing laws to the contrary notwithstanding , all private employers shall establish and provide sleeping quarters and/or facilities for their female employees and permit them to use such quarters after their working hours. Provided, that their working hours ends between eight o'clock at night to six o'clock in the morning of the following day.

rows.abstract: Any person who shall develop machines and technology that will improve the productivity and rural women workers shall be entitled to the following incentives: (1) Financial grant from the Department of Science and Technology for the fabrication of the model. rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE THE EFFICIENT AND EFFECTIVE DELIVERY OF CONVERGING COMMUNICATIONS SERVICES (convergence)
rows.abstract: "COVERGENCE" refers to the progressive integration of segments of the information and content industries, including telecommunicati ons, broadcasting, electronic commerce and data processing, into a single economic market based on distributed digital technology. > This bill, therefore, aims to propose a policy on convergence of the various technologies and means of communications and a long term strategic national development plan for the Philippines communications program. > In summary, it proposes the national policies and objectives for the promotion of convergent technology, as well as specific policies on aspects which shall effect the implementation of the same. It also proposed the rights of users as well as institutional responsibiilitie s to make the national convergence program viable. Finally it provides for penal provisions for violators.

rows.abstract: SUBJECT TO THE RIGHTS OF THE LAND BANK OF THE PHILIPPINES OVER  THE AWARDED LAND, ALL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS SHALL ACCEPT AS COLLATERAL FOR LOANS ANY DULY REGISTERED CERTIFICATE OF LAND OWNERSHIP AWARD ISSUED BY THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRARIAN REFORM; PROVIDED, THAT THE LOANS OBTAINED SHALL BE USED IN THE IMPROVEMENT OR DEVELOPMENT OF THE LAND AWARDED OR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF FACILITIES THAT WILL ENHANCE PRODUCTION OR MARKETING OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS OR WILL INCREASE FARM INCOME.

rows.abstract: The proposed measure aims to improve service standard by limiting the number of signatories required in government transactions and streamlining procedures to attain a smooth flow in the processing of papers and documents involved, with the end in view of expeditiously and effectively delivering basic services to the public. rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE CANCER CENTER, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The purposes and objectives of the Philippine Cancer Center are: (1) To construct, establish, operate and maintain an integrated medical insitution that will concentrate and specialiaze mainly on the multi-modality treatment of cancer and allied diseases; (2) To provide and extend medical services to the general public who are suffering from cance especially the poor and the less fortunate in life and relieve or alleviate their conditions from the afflictions of said disease; (3) To promote, encourage and engaged in medical and scientific researches on the early diagnosis, multi-modality treatment and prevention of cancer and gather, compile and publish such research finding for public information and dissemination; and (4) To encourage annd/or undertake the training of physicians, nurses, medical technicians, health officers and social workers on the scientific conduct of diagnosis, multi-modality treatment and prevention of cancer.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-11-28

rows.author: D021
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09290) enacted on 2004-04-15
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE FOOTWEAR, LEATHER AND TANNERY INDUSTRIES, PROVIDING INCENTIVES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Footwear, Leather and Tannery Industries Development Act of 2002." Rationale: The footwear, leather and tannery industries are three of the oldest industries in the country. Inextricably linked, a particular industry's problem tend to affect the others. Of late, these industries have been threatened by the influx of imports of competing products. Their problem is compounded by the lack of support services like marketing and brand protection for its manufacturers.> This bill aims to ensure notjust the survival but thedevelopment of said industries under a globalized environmen. It shall create a policy environment that will foster stronger linkages between these sectors by giving incentives for skills training and capital equipment acquissition and ensuring a ready market by requiring government employees to patronize products made by these domestic industries. It shall likewise encourage these industries to tap the export market to contribute to the country's dollar earnings.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05566

The proposed Code shall apply to all ships or vessels plying within the territorial waters of thePhilippines, whether domestic or foreign-owned, and to all Philippine flag vessels, except those owned and/or operated by the Philippine government or by foreign governments for military or non-commecial purposes, and unmotorized bancas, sailboats, and other water-borne contrivances less than three gross tons capacity.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE LOCAL HOUSING BOARDS IN EVERY CITY AND MUNICIPALITY PROVIDING FOR ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE SECTIONS 447 AND 458 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to establish a local housing board in every city and municipality. Under this bill, the Local Government Units, in coordination with other housing agencies, the private sectors and the NGOs are given the task to create a local housing framework that would adopt a continuing socialized housing program for the underprivileged and homeless urban and rural poor dwellers at affordable cost. > The bill also provides a mandatory subsidy to all government resettlement projects for the provision of infrastructure facilities and maintenance to be allocated proportionately in accordance with the area and number of population of the resettlement projects.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-12-03

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE REPRESENTATION OF COOPERATIVES IN THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE LAND BANK OF THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING THEREFOR REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3844, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is widely acknowledged that cooperatives play a crucial role in agrarian reform. The Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) was originally created to support the agrarian reform program and, as such, it has given prime importance to cooperatives in its effort to support agrarian reform and rural development. However, the cooperative sector is NOT represented in the LBP Board. This has deprived the cooperative sector of being heard in the policy-making body of the LBP. This bill seeksto remedy this situation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-12-03

rows.abstract: Rationale: Despite the unrelenting efforts of the Philippine National Police in their drive against the proliferation of illegal gambling, the social menace is not just lurking around the corner, it is staring at us in the eyes - that despite the existence of a law that imposes "stiffer" penalties to supposed violators and perpetuators of the things that contribute to our society's moral decay, bookie operations are rampant, jueteng is much visible, and so on. > This bill seeks to expand as well as respond with the changing environment.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 22, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE BOUNCING CHECK LAW
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to impose penalty upon any person who makes or draws and issues any check to apply on account or for value, knowing at the time of issue that he does not have sufficient funds in or credit with the drawee bank for the payment of suchcheck in full upon its presentment, which check is subsequently dishonored by the drawee bank for insufficiency of funds or credit or would have been dishonored for the same reason had not the drawer, without any valid reason, ordered the bank to stop payment, shall be punished by imprisonment of not less than thirty days but not more than one (1) year or by a fine of not less than but not more than double the amount of the check which fines shall in no case exceed Two Hundred Thousand Pesos, oor both such fine and imprisonment at the discretion of the court. > The first election for sectoral representatives in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Bayan and Sangguniang Panlungsod shall be held simultanteously with the local elections

rows.abstract: "Local Sectoral Representation Act of 2001". There shall be three (3) sectoral representatives each in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Bayan and Sangguniang Panlungsod who shall be elected pursuant to this Act: one (1) from the women sector; one (1) from the workers; and one (1) from any of the following sectors: the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, disabled persons and elderly, which may be determined by the sangguniang concerned not later than one (1) year prior to the holding of the next local elections: Provided, that, in the case of Sangguniang Panlalawigan, any of the sub-sectors of the workers may be considered as the second the third sector; Provided further that, the total number of elective positions in thelocal sanggunians shall not exceed the number of seats prescribed by law except in provinces, and in cities where sanggunian members are elected per district as provided by law. >

rows.abstract: All public and private schools shall include in their curricula the subject of human rights. No public or private schools shall be establish or allowed to operate unless human rights subjects are included in its curricula. > The Department of Education, Culture and Sports, in consultation with the Commission on Human Rights, shall take immediate steps to formulate courses on human rights curricual at all levels of education and training in both private and public schools in the country, adapting the scope and treatment of all subjects or courses on human rights to the respective educational levels.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE DEPARTMENT OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY TO PROVIDE EVERY BARANGAY TEN (10) PIECES OF STANDARDIZED METAL WEIGHTS WEIGHING ONE (1) KILOGRAM EACH TO BE PUT UNDER THE CUSTODY OF THE BARANGAY CAPTAIN AND LOANED FOR FREE TO ANY BARANGAY RESIDENT WHO WISHES TO CHECK THE ACCURACY OF THE WEIGHING SCALE BEING USED IN THE MARKETING OF ANY PRODUCT WHICH PRICE IS DETERMINED BY WEIGHT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The only effective solution to the problem is giving the consumers the power to ensure that the weighing instruments being used in the trade are "honest". This bill proposes to enforce the same by providing them a standardized metal weight a kilogram to allow them to check whether scales being used to weigh their products are, indeed, "honest". > This proposed will be most effective in the countryside especially to small fatmers who are marketing their produce. It will also save thegovernment time and money by doing away with regular inspections on the accuracy of weighing scales being used.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE USE OF NON-BIODEGRADAB LE PLASTIC MATERIALS AS CONTAINERS, BAGS, WRAPPERS OR PACKAGING FOR CONSUMER PRODUCTS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Plastic has taken its toll against our natural environment. It accounts for a great percentage of the urban and industrial waste in the country, most of which are disposed in rivers, esteros, seas, lakes and landfills. Discarded plastic could stay long in the environment and could create an adverse effect it not properly collected and disposed of. If thrown directly into the water, it could create aesthetic problems and may post navigational problems. It may damage the spawning grounds of fish and other aquatic fauna and flora. Plastic could clog the sewer lines and impair the pumping facilities and other equipment of the sewerage system. In farm lands, it may hinder water and air circulations in soil, thereby adversely affectinng plant growth and crop production.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2001-12-04

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 290 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991(RE: SHARE OF LGU's IN THE UTILIZATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE NATIONAL WEALTH WITHIN THEIR JURISDICTION)
rows.title_short: Amending RA 7160, Otherwise Known as the Local Government Code
rows.abstract: The Local Government Code is AMENDED as follows: Local government units shall, in addition to the internal revenue allotment, have a share of 40% of the gross collection derived (by the national government) from the preceding fiscal year from miningtaxes, royalties, forestry and fishery charges, and such other taxes, fees or charges, including related surcharges, interests, or fines, and from its share in any co-production, joint venture or production sharing agreement in the utilization and development of the national wealth within their territorial juridiction: Provided, that persons natural or juridical engaged in the utilization and development of the national wealth, shall pay directly the abovementioned 40% of their national wealthtaxes to the host local government units and the remaining 60% to the national government.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-03-18, transmitted to on 2003-03-19 and received by the Senate on 2003-03-21

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE OWNERSHIP, POSSESSION, IMPORTATION, SALE AND USE OF CHAINSAWS, PENALIZING VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: The Chainsaw Act of 2002
rows.abstract: "The Chain Saw Act of 2001". The bill provides for the requlation and monitoring of chain saws, beginning from its entry as imported equipment or importation of its parts for assembly in the country up to its final productive use. Importers, manufacturers, sellers, possessors, and users of chain saws are henceforth mandated to apply for appropriate permits from the DENR. The unauthorized possession use, sale, importation, including the defacement of the serial number of a chain saw are declaredunlawful with corresponding penalty of fine and imprisonment for their violation.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO HELP IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF EDUCATION IN THE COUNTRY BY ALLOWING PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS TO CONCENTRATE ON THEIR TEACHING DUTIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 13 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6646, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `THE ELECTION REFORM ACT OF 1987,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to amend Section 13 by authorizing the Commission of Elections to designate citizens preferably coming from the civic, youth, professional, educational, business and labor sectors to sit in the Board of Election Inspectors (BEI). Thesame guideliens shall be used in choosing the members of the Election Registration of Board of Canvassers, and the canvassing committes. This way, all citizens regardless of their professions or calling shall share the equal burden of ensuring free,orderly, honest, peaceful and credible elections. It also promotes volunteerism, especially among the youth, which is one of the hallmarks of a republic and democracy such as ours.

rows.author: C130
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING AND REAFFIRMING THE COCO LEVY FUNDS AND ASSETS AS PUBLIC FUND AND CREATING THE PRESIDENTIAL COCONUT INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT COUNCIL FOR PURPOSES OF MANAGEMENT THEREOF
rows.abstract: "Coco Levy Funds and Assets Are Public Funds Act of 2001". Rationale: The nature of the funds has been the subject of a legal battle between the government and the private corporations and entities utilizing the coco levy funds. As a consequence, the funds could not be utilized and were in fact not used for the benefit of their true owners, the coconut farmers. It is ironic that after almost fifteen (15) years, the cases related to the coco levy scam had never been concretely resolved in our courts to the great disadvantage of millions of small coconut farmers and farm workers from whom the levy was collected.> This bill was filed for Congress to finally declare and affirm the coco levy funds and assets as public funds so they can be accesssed and appropriate programs could be funded for the benefit of their true owners and of the entire industry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-12-10
